collections.name: For younger kids
collections.description: Children playing, animals and bright color, with poems written for children.

collections.name: For older kids and adults
collections.description: People reading, talking and making things, with Thoreau, Emerson and other writers.

collections.name: Famous photographs
collections.description: The first flight, the Empire State Building going up, the Earth seen from the Moon.

picture.title: A Holiday
picture.licence: Public domain (CC0), Art Institute of Chicago
picture.about: Edward Potthast painted children playing at the edge of the sea on a windy day. Sunny beach scenes like this were what he was best known for.

words.text: When I was down beside the sea / A wooden spade they gave to me / To dig the sandy shore.
words.work: At the Sea-Side, in A Child’s Garden of Verses

picture.title: Five Young Boys Rolling a Large Snowball
picture.licence: Public domain (CC0), Art Institute of Chicago
picture.about: A Japanese woodblock print from about 1772. Each color was carved into its own block of wood and printed one after another, by hand.

words.text: What are you able to build with your blocks? / Castles and palaces, temples and docks.
words.work: Block City, in A Child’s Garden of Verses

picture.title: Florida Jay
picture.maker: Robert Havell, after John James Audubon
picture.licence: Public domain (CC0), Art Institute of Chicago
picture.about: From The Birds of America, John James Audubon’s book of birds drawn life-size. Robert Havell engraved Audubon’s painting, and every print was colored by hand.

words.text: “Hope” is the thing with feathers — / That perches in the soul —

picture.title: Houses at Murnau
picture.licence: Public domain (CC0), Art Institute of Chicago
picture.about: Kandinsky painted the houses of Murnau, a small town in Bavaria near the Alps, in colors brighter than life. A few years later he was painting pictures with no houses in them at all.

picture.title: Winter: Cat on a Cushion
picture.licence: Public domain (CC0), Art Institute of Chicago
picture.about: Théophile-Alexandre Steinlen loved cats and drew them again and again. In this color print, called Winter, one keeps warm on a cushion.

words.text: There is no Frigate like a Book / To take us Lands away

picture.title: Croquet Scene
picture.licence: Public domain (CC0), Art Institute of Chicago
picture.about: Croquet had only just come to America from Britain when Winslow Homer painted this game in the afternoon sun. It is one of five paintings he made of it.

words.text: The world is so full of a number of things, / I’m sure we should all be as happy as kings.
words.work: Happy Thought, in A Child’s Garden of Verses

picture.title: Boats on the Beach at Étretat
picture.licence: Public domain (CC0), Art Institute of Chicago
picture.about: Rain kept Claude Monet indoors, so he painted these fishing boats on the beach at Étretat, in France, from his hotel window.

words.text: Believe me, my young friend, there is nothing — absolutely nothing — half so much worth doing as simply messing about in boats.

picture.title: Equestrienne
picture.licence: Public domain (CC0), Art Institute of Chicago
picture.about: A woman riding her horse, shaped in clay in China about 1,300 years ago. Figures like this were placed in the tombs of wealthy families, showing the fashions and pastimes they enjoyed.

picture.title: Water Lily Pond
picture.licence: Public domain (CC0), Art Institute of Chicago
picture.about: Monet turned a marsh behind his house at Giverny, in France, into a pond with water lilies and a Japanese-style bridge. He painted it for the rest of his life.

words.text: Who has seen the wind? / Neither I nor you: / But when the leaves hang trembling, / The wind is passing through.
It is not enough to be industrious; so are the ants. What are you industrious about?
words.work: a letter to H. G. O. Blake

picture.title: Woman before an Aquarium
picture.licence: Public domain (CC0), Art Institute of Chicago
picture.about: Henri Matisse painted this while living in Nice, in the south of France. The patterned screen behind her echoes the Islamic art he had seen on trips to Algeria and Morocco.

words.text: What is this life if, full of care, / We have no time to stand and stare.

picture.title: The Conversation
picture.licence: Public domain (CC0), Art Institute of Chicago
picture.about: Marcellin Desboutin painted and made prints in Paris, where his friends included the painters Edgar Degas and Édouard Manet.

words.text: The only way to have a friend is to be one.

picture.title: The Herring Net
picture.licence: Public domain (CC0), Art Institute of Chicago
picture.about: Two fishermen haul in a net full of herring while their small boat rides the swell. Winslow Homer painted it in Prouts Neck, Maine, where he lived by the sea.

words.text: Let us, then, be up and doing, / With a heart for any fate; / Still achieving, still pursuing, / Learn to labor and to wait.

picture.title: Painting with Green Center
picture.licence: Public domain (CC0), Art Institute of Chicago
picture.about: Kandinsky was one of the first painters to leave out things you can name and let color and shape do the work, the way music does without words.

picture.title: “Germantown Eye-Dazzler” Rug
picture.licence: Public domain (CC0), Art Institute of Chicago
picture.about: Navajo (Diné) weavers made bright rugs in this style, called Eye Dazzler, in the late 1800s, with dyed yarn from Germantown, Pennsylvania. Every zigzag is woven by hand.

words.text: Little strokes fell great oaks.

picture.title: Interrupted Reading
picture.licence: Public domain (CC0), Art Institute of Chicago
picture.about: Camille Corot was famous for his landscapes, but late in life he also painted people in his studio, like this woman looking up from her book.

words.text: Read the best books first, or you may not have a chance to read them at all.
words.work: A Week on the Concord and Merrimack Rivers

picture.title: An Artist at His Easel
picture.licence: Public domain (CC0), Art Institute of Chicago
picture.about: A watercolor by John Singer Sargent of a painter at work outdoors. Famous for his portraits, Sargent spent his summers painting watercolors like this one.

words.text: To travel hopefully is a better thing than to arrive, and the true success is to labour.

picture.title: The Song of the Lark
picture.licence: Public domain (CC0), Art Institute of Chicago
picture.about: A girl stops work in the fields at sunrise to listen to a lark singing. In 1934 it was voted “America’s Best Loved Picture” in a Chicago newspaper’s contest.

words.text: Rest is not idleness, and to lie sometimes on the grass under trees on a summer’s day, listening to the murmur of the water, or watching the clouds float across the blue sky, is by no means a waste of time.

picture.title: Lozenge Composition with Yellow, Black, Blue, Red, and Gray
picture.licence: Public domain (CC0), Art Institute of Chicago
picture.about: Piet Mondrian made paintings from straight black lines and a few colors, moving them until they balanced. He turned this square canvas on its corner to make a diamond.

picture.title: The first flight, Kitty Hawk
picture.licence: Public domain
picture.about: The first flight of a powered airplane: Orville Wright at the controls, Wilbur running alongside. It lasted 12 seconds. The man who took the picture had never used a camera before.

words.text: If you are looking for perfect safety, you will do well to sit on a fence and watch the birds; but if you really wish to learn, you must mount a machine and become acquainted with its tricks by actual trial.

picture.title: High on the Empire State Building, N.Y.
picture.licence: Public domain (CC0), Art Institute of Chicago
picture.about: Lewis Hine followed the workers up the Empire State Building as it rose, photographing them high above New York. The building opened in 1931.

words.text: If you have built castles in the air, your work need not be lost; that is where they should be. Now put the foundations under them.

picture.title: Power house mechanic working on steam pump
picture.licence: Public domain
picture.about: Lewis Hine made “work portraits” like this to show the skilled people who build machines and keep them running. His earlier photographs of children at work helped change the laws.

picture.title: The Tetons and the Snake River
picture.maker: Ansel Adams, for the National Park Service
picture.licence: Public domain
picture.about: Ansel Adams took this in Grand Teton National Park, in Wyoming, for the National Park Service. In 1977 it was sent into space on the Voyager Golden Record.

words.text: In every walk with nature one receives far more than he seeks.

picture.title: The Horse in Motion
picture.licence: Public domain
picture.about: Does a galloping horse ever have all four hooves off the ground? Eadweard Muybridge set up a row of cameras to find out, and it does.

picture.title: Snowflakes
picture.licence: Public domain
picture.about: Wilson Bentley, a Vermont farmer, caught snowflakes on black velvet and photographed them through a microscope before they melted. He photographed more than 5,000.

words.text: How full of the creative genius is the air in which these are generated! I should hardly admire more if real stars fell and lodged on my coat.

picture.title: Earthrise
picture.licence: Public domain
picture.about: The Earth rising over the Moon, seen by the crew of Apollo 8, the first people to fly around the Moon. William Anders took it on Christmas Eve, 1968.

picture.title: Buzz Aldrin on the Moon
picture.licence: Public domain
picture.about: Buzz Aldrin on the Moon during Apollo 11. Neil Armstrong took the picture, and you can see him and their lunar module reflected in Aldrin’s visor.

words.text: To strive, to seek, to find, and not to yield.

picture.title: The Blue Marble
picture.licence: Public domain
picture.about: The whole Earth, lit by the Sun behind the crew of Apollo 17 on their way to the Moon. It is one of the most reproduced pictures in history.

picture.title: Bruce McCandless II on the first untethered spacewalk
picture.licence: Public domain
picture.about: Bruce McCandless floats free in space, tied to nothing, on the first untethered spacewalk. He steered with a jet pack called the Manned Maneuvering Unit.

picture.title: Pillars of Creation, the Eagle Nebula
picture.licence: Public domain
picture.about: Towers of gas and dust in the Eagle Nebula, about 6,500 light-years away, where new stars are being born. The Hubble Space Telescope took it in 1995.

words.text: To see a World in a Grain of Sand / And a Heaven in a Wild Flower, / Hold Infinity in the palm of your hand / And Eternity in an hour.

picture.title: Curiosity’s self-portrait on Mars
picture.licence: Public domain
picture.about: NASA’s Curiosity rover on Mars, in a self-portrait put together from dozens of pictures taken by a camera on its arm.
